title: INDEX MATCH vs XLOOKUP
description: See how the flexible INDEX/MATCH combination compares to the modern XLOOKUP function.
intro: INDEX combined with MATCH was the most flexible lookup method before XLOOKUP existed. It can look left, right, and handle dynamic ranges. XLOOKUP now provides similar power with simpler syntax.

comparisonTable.functionA: Fast with small datasets; can be slower than XLOOKUP on very large ranges
Easy with row and column MATCH

whenToUseA: Use INDEX/MATCH when you need maximum compatibility with older Excel versions or when you need a 2D lookup with separate row and column match.
whenToUseB: Use XLOOKUP when it is available and you want cleaner, more maintainable formulas.
verdict: XLOOKUP is generally preferred for new work, but INDEX/MATCH remains essential for backward compatibility and complex 2D lookups.

faq.question: Is INDEX MATCH obsolete?
faq.answer: No, it is still widely used and works in all Excel versions.

faq.question: Can XLOOKUP do 2D lookup?
faq.answer: Yes, by returning an array and matching both dimensions, but INDEX/MATCH is often simpler for 2D.
